question:
A full-wave bridge rectifier is connected to a transformer secondary of $12\,\text{V}_{rms}$ at $50\,\text{Hz}$. The load draws approximately constant current $I_L=0.10\,\text{A}$. A capacitor filter is to be connected across the load to reduce ripple.

Assume each conducting diode has a forward drop of $0.70\,\text{V}$; two diodes conduct in a bridge. Let the ripple frequency be $f_r=2f$.

Use the approximation for a capacitor-input filter:</br>

$\Delta V_{pp}\approx \frac{I_L}{f_r C}.$

(a) Compute the peak of secondary voltage $V_m$ and the peak available across the filter capacitor $V_p\approx V_m-2(0.70)$.

(b) Design the minimum capacitance $C$ such that $\Delta V_{pp}\le 0.50\,\text{V}$.

(c) Estimate the average dc output using</br>

$V_{dc}\approx V_p-\frac{\Delta V_{pp}}{2}.$

(d) Determine the minimum PIV rating required for each diode in a bridge rectifier in terms of $V_m$, and compute its value here.

(e) Draw the bridge rectifier circuit with capacitor filter and sketch the output waveform showing ripple ($\Delta V_{pp}$) clearly.

Present the final designed values and reasoning.

options.A: $V_m\approx 16.97\,\text{V}$, $V_p\approx 15.57\,\text{V}$; $C_{min}=2000\,\mu\text{F}$ so a standard choice is $2200\,\mu\text{F}$; $V_{dc}\approx 15.32\,\text{V}$; for bridge $\text{PIV}\approx V_m\approx 17\,\text{V}$ per diode.
options.C: $V_m\approx 16.97\,\text{V}$, $V_p\approx 15.57\,\text{V}$; $C_{min}=2000\,\mu\text{F}$; but $V_{dc}$ must equal $12\,\text{V}$ because transformer is $12\,\text{V}_{rms}$; $\text{PIV}=0$ because the capacitor blocks reverse voltage.
